# Scheduling Requirements Checklist: Feature 005

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency, and testability of Feature 005 scheduling requirements, with emphasis on recurrence/timezone semantics and API concurrency.
**Created**: 2026-09-29
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the states “no schedule,” “configured but disabled,” and “configured and enabled” defined consistently across schedule reads, status display, and preview behavior? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-011, §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK002 Are default values for newly created schedules, including the initial enabled state, stated consistently as user requirements or explicitly identified as an assumption? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK003 Are all recurrence-specific requirements complete, including daily frequency, one ISO weekday for weekly, and day 1–31 with month-end clamping for monthly schedules? [Coverage, Spec §FR-003–FR-005]
- [ ] CHK004 Are requirements for the supported timezone set, its selection by users, and what happens when a previously accepted timezone is no longer supported complete? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK005 Are user-facing accessibility requirements for recurrence controls, timezone selection, validation feedback, schedule status, and preview adequately specified? [Gap, Constitution Principle XI]
- [ ] CHK006 Are requirements complete for previewing an unsaved candidate, including how invalid candidates and disabled candidates are represented without persisting them? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011, §FR-018, §FR-021]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 Is “the next occurrence” unambiguous for every recurrence when its resolved local wall time is equal to or earlier than the supplied reference instant? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK008 Are the DST gap and overlap rules specific enough to determine a unique instant for all supported timezone transitions, not only one-hour transitions? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the meaning and precision of execution time clear, including whether seconds or fractional seconds are invalid rather than rounded? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK010 Is “named timezone” precise enough to distinguish accepted IANA identifiers from fixed offsets, aliases, and browser-local timezone defaults? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK011 Are the terminology and formatting requirements for “next scheduled occurrence” clear enough to prevent users interpreting a preview as a guaranteed execution? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, §FR-020]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK012 Are recurrence field clearing rules consistent between recurrence changes in the UI, complete replacement requests, and persisted schedule invariants? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, US1 Scenario 5]
- [ ] CHK013 Are schedule enabled state and Monitoring Configuration enabled state consistently independent in creation, editing, removal, and status display requirements? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014–FR-016, US3]
- [ ] CHK014 Are preview rules consistent for absent schedules, disabled schedules, enabled schedules, candidate previews, and persisted schedule reads? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010–FR-011]
- [ ] CHK015 Does the stale-update requirement align with the API contract’s chosen HTTP status and conditional-update semantics without requiring a client-visible revision in the schedule DTO? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021; Plan §API and preview]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK016 Can SC-001 be evaluated objectively for each recurrence and the preservation of unrelated configuration, without relying on subjective usability judgments? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK017 Are the expected reference instants, timezone, recurrence inputs, and expected outcomes sufficiently defined for independently reproducible daily, weekly, monthly, leap-year, and DST acceptance cases? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002–SC-004, §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK018 Are the stale-save acceptance conditions measurable, including which save wins, how stale state is identified, and what remains available to the user after conflict? [Measurability, Spec §FR-021, §SC-008]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK019 Are recovery requirements clear when saving or removing a schedule fails, including whether drafts are retained and how users reconcile after a stale-write conflict? [Recovery, Spec §FR-018, §FR-021, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK020 Are deletion/removal requirements complete for configured and absent schedules, repeated removal, and concurrent removal or replacement? [Coverage, Spec §FR-012, §FR-016, §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK021 Are month-end, leap-year, year-boundary, UTC-date-boundary, exact-reference equality, and timezone transition cases all covered without conflicting recurrence rules? [Edge Case Coverage, Spec §FR-005, §FR-008–FR-009]
- [ ] CHK022 Are requirements explicit for preserving credentials, scope, configuration enabled state, and other fields through schedule create, replace, failed mutation, and removal? [Coverage, Spec §FR-015–FR-017, §SC-005]

## Non-Functional Requirements and Scope

- [ ] CHK023 Are the preview’s freshness expectations and any acceptable delay between editing candidate values and showing the calculated result specified clearly enough for consistent UX? [Clarity, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK024 Are all exclusions from Feature 005 consistently bounded so preview/calculation cannot be confused with scheduler eligibility, execution creation, or mining behavior? [Scope, Spec §FR-023, §SC-007]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK025 Are timezone database availability, supported-timezone catalogue ownership, and the effect of timezone database updates documented as explicit assumptions or requirements? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions; Plan §Domain and recurrence calculation]
- [ ] CHK026 Is the future Feature 009 relationship clearly identified as a deferred dependency rather than behavior required of Feature 005? [Dependency, Spec §FR-023; Plan §Deferred to Feature 009]

## Ambiguities and Conflicts

- [ ] CHK027 Is the API outcome for a stale schedule update stated consistently in the spec and API contract (including whether it is HTTP 409 or 412)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-021; Plan §API and preview]
- [ ] CHK028 Is the expected behavior after an uncertain client/network response to a successful schedule write defined, especially whether a retry is conditional on the prior ETag and how the client discovers the committed state? [Gap, Spec §FR-021]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`; it was not modified.
- `tasks.md` was not present when this checklist was generated; items are grounded in `spec.md`, `plan.md`, and the API contract.
